newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian NLB bank's 1996 pre-tax profit jumps.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian NLB bank's 1996 pre-tax profit jumps.

text.p: Slovenia's largest bank, state-owned Nova Ljubljanska banka d.d. (NLB) on Wednesday announced a 94 percent jump in its preliminary pre-tax earnings for 1996.
NLB said its unaudited pre-tax profit almost doubled to 8.0 billion tolars ($52.6 million) in 1996 from 4.1 billion in previous year.
"Our business results have been improving constantly since 1993 when the rehabilitation process started," NLB chief executive Marko Voljc told a news conference.
He traced higher profits to a 27 percent growth in deposits, a 17 percent increase in loans and a decline in debts with the Bank of Slovenia to 2.1 billion tolars from 15.6 billion.
The bank's balance sheet assets in 1996 rose to 490.4 billion tolars ($3.2 billion) from 431 billion tolars in 1995. That represented an unchanged domestic market share of 27 percent.
"Balance sheet assets are expected to increase by another 15 percent this year, when we anticipate the rehabilitation will finish," said NLB board-member Boris Zakrajsek.

The privatisation scheme for NLB and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor d.d, the only two state-owned banks out of a total of 28 banks in Slovenia, has not been determined yet. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
